text:
marco_sales: Need a hosted API key setup for a week-long POC with MeridianHealth. Requirements: IP allowlist, scopes limited to embeddings + chat_generation, keys rotated every 24h, and audit export to their S3. No dashboard access. Who can provision and what's the quick flow?
eli: We can do short-lived hosted POC keys. Two options: (A) one-time provisioning URL that mints a 24h token for them to self-claim, (B) server-side scheduled rotation where we push new keys to them. Need org_id + CIDRs + desired TTL. Confirm if they want KMS-backed keys and SIEM export.
marco_sales: Org ID MH-442. CIDRs: 18.200.0.0/16 and 13.37.13.37/32. They want keys KMS-backed and no console.
jane_security: @eli confirm that each key has metadata (provisioned_by, poc_id, sales_deal) and revocation is immediate with an API we can call. Also need 90d audit retention and proof of revocation for their compliance team.
eli: Yes — keys are KMS-wrapped and carry metadata. Revocation via DELETE /v1/poc-keys/:id requires service account token; revocation events are logged with actor and timestamp. Default enterprise retention is 365d but we can set POC buckets to 90d.
samir: Cost question: embedding-heavy tests — will this be billed regularly? Any way to pre-apply credits?
eli: Hosted POC usage is billed standard; we can preload trial credits against the org for the duration. Give me an estimated token/embedding volume and we can size credits. Rotation itself is negligible cost.
marco_sales: They also want an automated rotate button their infra can call. Can we give them a one-time provisioning link that mints scoped tokens and also an endpoint to request a new one without human ops?
eli: Yes. Flow: create a scoped template -> generate a one-time provisioning URL (or a short-lived client credential tied to their IP allowlist) -> they call it to receive a token. For self-service rotation, we can issue a client credential bound to allowed CIDRs and scope that can call /v1/poc-keys/mint to get new 24h tokens. We can set strict rate limits.
infra-bot: create-template tpl-mh-2026 {"scopes":["chat","embeddings"],"allowed_cidrs":["18.200.0.0/16","13.37.13.37/32"],"no_console":true} -> success (tpl-mh-2026)
eli: I'll provision an initial demo key for the sync tomorrow 09:00 PST and post the one-time URL here. Tagging it meridian-poc-demo-2026-03-23. TTL 24h.
infra-bot: Key created (id: poc-112233), tags: [meridian-poc-demo-2026-03-23], expires: 2026-03-24T16:00:00Z, revocation_endpoint: https://api.redwood.com/v1/poc-keys/poc-112233
infra-bot: Provisioning URL (one-time): https://auth.redwood.com/p/one-time/def456 1NOTE: link expires on first use or after 24h
marco_sales: Great. I'll send this during the kickoff. Runbook I'll share: 1) use link to claim token, 2) tokens auto-expire in 24h, 3) for rotation they can call our mint endpoint with the client credential or request new one-time link, 4) confirm IP allowlist, 5) logs exported to their S3 bucket daily.
jane_security: Add me to the offboard checklist: confirm revoke + export snapshot of logs at time of offboard.
eli: Done. I'll enable SIEM export to s3://meridian-poc-logs and attach service_account sales-poc-provisioner in the token metadata. I'll also add a webhook for revocation receipts so we can hand them proof.
marco_sales: Thanks all. If anything blocks, ping me. :thumbsup:
eli: One more note for engineering: when you mint via client credential, include header X-Provisioned-By: sales-poc-provisioner so audit logs are searchable.
samir: Acknowledged, will relay to their infra contact.
